newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian supreme court says Socialists win town.
newsitem.headline: Serbian supreme court says Socialists win town.

text.p: The Serbian Supreme Court declared on Monday that President Slobodan Milosevic's party had won disputed elections in the town of Sabac.

The ruling flew in the face of an independent international investigation that verified the opposition coalition's claim to victory in Sabac and 13 other towns where the ruling Socialists annulled elections, claiming "irregularities".

The Supreme Court ruling was the second serious blow in hours to the opposition's protest campaign to reinstate its municipal election triumphs, verified by investigators from the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Earlier in the day, the Belgrade municipal court suspended a week-old election commission ruling that the Socialists had lost the elections in Yugoslavia's capital.

Municipal justices asked the Supreme Court to decide what court should rule on a Socialist appeal against the commission decision in what analysts described as an effort to evade responsibility at the local level.
The Supreme Court ruled that the Socialists had won 35 town assembly seats in Sabac and the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition 29 with the other five mandates taken by small parties.
